copies.headline: Grant's Backfield Brings a Knife to Adam's Gun Range
copies.body:
This is a running back game and Grant doesn't have one. Adam's best two, Kenneth Walker III and Bucky Irving, project 39 to Grant's 25, and the game scripts cooperate: Walker in a Chiefs offense favored by 10 is the exact situation where a team sits on a lead and hands it off, while Irving gets a 47.5 total in Chicago with Tampa chasing from six down. Grant counters with Quinshon Judkins at New Orleans in a 42.5-total slog and Jadarian Price. Omarion Hampton at nine is a third option, not a solution.
Receiver is where Grant stays alive — Amon-Ra St. Brown in a 50.5-point game at Miami is the single best spot on either roster, and Zay Flowers gets volume as a 10-point underdog. But Christian Watson is questionable, Brian Thomas Jr. projects seven, and Brock Purdy against Las Vegas in a 52.5 total tops Mahomes. Adam leads the league at 139.6 a game with a 75% all-play; Grant is 48% and middling.

copies.headline: Logan's Backfield Is A Rumor, CJ's Isn't
copies.body:
Logan is the better team by every season-long metric — 122.4 per game, 54-34 all-play, 3-5 only because the schedule has mugged him for nearly two wins — and he's still probably losing this one at running back. His best two backs project for 20 combined: Zach Charbonnet in a 39.5-total game Seattle will favor by 8.5, plus Tyler Allgeier or Braelon Allen. Jaylen Warren is a zero, Jeremiyah Love and Jacory Croskey-Merritt are on IR. CJ counters with Jonathan Taylor in a 51.5-total shootout against Dallas, Chuba Hubbard, and Ollie Gordon II in a game Miami trails by a touchdown in. That's 38 against 20, and no lineup shuffle closes it.
Logan's answer is the pass game: Joe Burrow in Atlanta with a 52.5 total, Justin Jefferson chasing Buffalo, Luther Burden and Tetairoa McMillan, plus Isaiah Likely. That's +18 across QB/WR/TE. It's enough to make this close, not enough to win it, and CJ's receiving corps is genuinely thin — Rashee Rice, Parker Washington, a questionable Emeka Egbuka, Alec Pierce on IR, DK Metcalf at zero. If Egbuka sits, this tightens fast.

copies.headline: Kaleb's 5-3 Record Finally Meets Its Audit
copies.body:
Kaleb is the luckiest 5-3 in the league — 103.4 points per game, dead last, with a 34-54 all-play and a +1.9 luck number that reads like a confession. Christian scores 126.5 (3rd), has lost five games anyway, and holds the edge at every position: 20-19 at quarterback, 32-26 at running back, 46-38 at the top three receivers, 16-12 at tight end. That's roughly a 19-point gap before anything breaks, and the breaks lean Christian too. Kaleb's backfield is Ashton Jeanty as a 10-point road dog at San Francisco and a questionable Breece Hall with RJ Harvey on IR behind him. If Hall sits, there is nothing there.
Christian's spots are better football. CeeDee Lamb and Brandon Aubrey in a 51.5-total game at Indianapolis, George Kittle in a 52.5 against the Raiders, Chase Brown in Atlanta's 52.5. Trevor Lawrence as a 10-point favorite in a 40.5 is the one soft landing, but Jordan Love is sitting right there. Kaleb's ceiling is Drake London in the Cincinnati shootout and Harold Fannin in a 42.5 at New Orleans, which isn't a plan so much as a hope.

copies.headline: Leif's Backfield Outnumbers Noah's Entire Roster
copies.body:
The margin lives at running back, where Leif can throw out Christian McCaffrey (23) and still have Woody Marks and Derrick Henry at 14 apiece as the next men up. That depth matters because McCaffrey is questionable, and San Francisco's 52.5 total against Las Vegas — the highest on the board, with the Niners laying 10 — means whoever gets the carries there is working in the best scoring environment of the week. Noah's RB2 is Rhamondre Stevenson at 12, and after that it's Mike Washington Jr. at 7. There is no insulation.
Noah's edges are real but tiny: Drake Maye over Josh Allen by a point, Colston Loveland over Kyle Pitts by two. The receiver rooms project even at 37, except Noah's version requires Michael Wilson and Garrett Wilson, both questionable, in games Arizona and the Jets are losing by 8.5 and 10. Chasing points is Noah's only path. Leif is running a 2-6 schedule's worth of luck, but he's got the better roster underneath it.

copies.headline: Mitchell's Kicker Is On IR, Everything Else Too
copies.body:
Mitchell actually wins the skill-position math on paper — Jahmyr Gibbs (26 proj, Lions favored by seven in a 50.5 game) plus Dak in a 51.5-total shootout at Indy gives him a QB-RB edge of eight. The problem is everywhere else. There's no kicker on the roster at all with Tyler Loop on IR, that's a zero in a starting slot, and DJ Moore is questionable with Christian Kirk's one projected point as the fallback. John answers with tight end: Brock Bowers plus Trey McBride, a six-point edge over Tyler Warren, and Bowers gets the Raiders as ten-point dogs in a 52.5-total game in San Francisco, which is the exact script that produces 20 targets of garbage-time volume.
John's receiver room is thinner than the ranks suggest — Puka Nacua carries it and DeMario Douglas is the WR2 — but he has three usable quarterbacks and five running backs to Mitchell's two healthy ones. John is 133.0 per game, second in scoring, 61-27 all-play, and coming off 165.1. Mitchell is dead last in all-play at 30-58 and hasn't cleared 110 in three weeks.

copies.headline: Peter's Quarterback Room Is A Rumor
copies.body:
This comes down to receiver and quarterback, and Isaac wins both rooms even if the top-line projections say otherwise. Ja'Marr Chase in a 52.5-total game at Atlanta is the single best asset on either side, and Malik Nabers gets Philadelphia in a 38.5-point game where the Giants will be throwing from behind by the third quarter. Isaac's best three wideouts project 51 to Peter's 42, and that gap widens because Peter is starting Malik Willis with Lamar Jackson out and Justin Herbert facing a Houston defense in a 40.5-total slog. Willis is a 17-point projection built on garbage-time hope — Miami is a 7-point dog to Detroit, so the volume is real, the efficiency is not.
Peter's edge is the backfield, and it's only four points: Bijan Robinson and Josh Jacobs against Javonte Williams and whatever Cam Skattebo's ankle allows. Behind them it's Kyle Monangai and Brian Robinson Jr., both questionable, which is not depth so much as a prayer. Tee Higgins in the same shootout as Chase keeps this close, but A.J. Brown at zero and Romeo Doubs on IR means Peter is running Denzel Boston out there as a WR3. Isaac's roster is deeper everywhere it matters, and Peter's 69.8-point Week 6 is the floor that's still lurking.

intro: Grant at Adam is the one to watch: Adam has the thinnest edge on the board and a loss drops him out of the 6-2 tie at the top while handing Grant a path back into the playoff picture. Isaac at Peter carries the most weight below that line — Peter's 5-3 is doing a lot of work holding off a crowded 4-4 logjam, and Isaac is favored to shove him into it. Then there's John at Mitchell, where the biggest mismatch on the slate meets the only man in the league who could lose to a bye week.
